description:
Implement the RFC 8620 §7.2 PushSubscription server-side surface in jmap-server. Currently absent: no PushSubscriptionBackend trait, no register_push_subscription_handlers function, no handle_push_subscription_* handlers, no generate_verification_code method.

RFC 8620 §7.2 requires:
- PushSubscription/get
- PushSubscription/set
- A verificationCode flow: on create with non-empty url and keys, the server generates an unguessable verificationCode, POSTs it to the client URL, and the client patches it back to prove receipt.

CRITICAL CONSTRAINT (forward-looking placeholder bead bd:JMAP-sc1b.101):

The verificationCode is credential-grade material. The PushSubscriptionBackend trait method that mints it MUST follow the workspace rule documented in crate-jmap-server/AGENTS.md 'Backend trait rule: secret-minting methods require CSPRNG':

1. Doc comment MUST require a CSPRNG verbatim (e.g. OsRng / getrandom).
2. Reference MemoryBackend impl MUST actually use OsRng / getrandom in production builds, not a timestamp or counter.

Precedent: bd:JMAP-sc1b.78 (invite code CSPRNG trait doc), bd:JMAP-sc1b.93 (the matching reference-impl audit).

Scope (estimated):
- PushSubscriptionBackend trait + types (~150 LOC)
- handle_push_subscription_get / _set / _changes / _query handlers (~300 LOC)
- Reference MemoryBackend impl with OsRng-derived verificationCode (~100 LOC)
- Integration tests (~250 LOC) including a regression test that the verification code passes the same CSPRNG-canary properties bd:JMAP-sc1b.93 codified (no duplicates across 256 samples, max shared prefix < 10).
- Wiring into register_jmap_core_handlers (or equivalent dispatch registration).

Total ~800 LOC including tests, plus minor wiring in jmap-server lib.rs.

Acceptance:
- All four RFC 8620 §7.2 methods implemented and dispatched.
- generate_verification_code trait doc carries the CSPRNG warning verbatim from AGENTS.md.
- MemoryBackend impl uses getrandom::getrandom (already a per-crate dev-dep in chat-server via the bd:JMAP-sc1b.93 fix path; extend to jmap-server as needed).
- Regression test confirms verification codes pass the canary properties from invite_code_is_csprng.

Closes the forward-looking bd:JMAP-sc1b.101 by being the concrete work item it gestures at.
notes:
De-labeling human (2026-05-11, Mark): implementation feature, no pending design decision. Constraints are documented in the bead body (RFC 8620 §7.2 scope; CSPRNG via OsRng/getrandom per workspace 'Backend trait rule' in crate-jmap-server/AGENTS.md). Autonomous /do-beads loop can pick this up.
Stopping before implementation per /do-beads escalation rule.

Pre-claim assessment (2026-05-12 do-beads session):

Bead description estimates ~800 LOC across 5 distinct sub-pieces:
  1. PushSubscriptionBackend trait + types in jmap-server (~150 LOC)
  2. handle_push_subscription_get / _set / _changes / _query handlers (~300 LOC)
  3. Reference MemoryBackend impl with OsRng-derived verificationCode (~100 LOC)
  4. Integration tests (~250 LOC) including the CSPRNG canary regression test
  5. Wiring into the dispatcher registration path (small)

This is multi-session work for one autonomous claim. The CSPRNG canary
regression test (slice 4) cross-references bd:JMAP-sc1b.93 patterns
and is security-critical — needs careful review per the workspace
Backend-trait-CSPRNG rule in crate-jmap-server/AGENTS.md.

Also discovered during scope check: jmap-server today has no tests/
directory and no MemoryBackend (other foundation crates also lack
one — MemoryBackend pattern is per-extension-server). Slice 3 would
need to decide where the reference impl lives (src/memory.rs behind a
feature flag is the chat-server pattern; jmap-server has no precedent
yet) and slice 4 needs to introduce a tests/ scaffold. These are
not-quite-trivial scope expansions hidden inside the original
estimate.

Recommended decomposition (file 5 child beads, work slice 1 first):

  .107.1 — PushSubscriptionBackend trait + RFC 8620 §7.2 types
  .107.2 — handle_push_subscription_{get,set,changes,query[Changes]} handlers
  .107.3 — Reference MemoryBackend impl + getrandom dev-dep (matches
           bd:JMAP-sc1b.93 chat-server pattern)
  .107.4 — Integration tests (incl. CSPRNG canary) + tests/ scaffold
  .107.5 — Dispatcher wiring + register_push_subscription_handlers

Alternative: leave atomic and have a single contributor with full
context land it in two sessions.

Decision belongs to Mark. Labelling 'human' so the loop does not
re-pick this. Releasing claim back to open.
Decision (2026-05-11, Mark): γ-defer — close as out-of-scope for publish-readiness.

Rationale: workspace identity is 'library kit for building JMAP servers and clients in Rust'. PushSubscription server-side (RFC 8620 §7.2) is a foundation-method-implementer surface, and a reference MemoryBackend for it would mean foundation grows into a method-implementer with state + tests scaffolding — a posture shift the workspace has deliberately avoided.

PushSubscription delivery (server pushes verificationCode to a client-supplied URL) is one of three RFC 8620 push mechanisms. The workspace exercises the other two (SSE per RFC 8620 §7.3 in jmap-base-client; WebSocket per RFC 8887 in jmap-base-client). The workspace's own test surface (jmap-testjig, JMAP-cf7p) does not need §7.2; SSE + WS are sufficient.

Future consumers of the kit who need to implement §7.2 server-side (e.g. webhook-style delivery for mobile clients via APNs/FCM) implement against the JmapBackend trait themselves. The forward-looking CSPRNG constraint that JMAP-sc1b.101 captured (closed) survives in workspace AGENTS.md from the JMAP-sc1b.78 / .93 work — any future PushSubscriptionBackend implementer will encounter the workspace 'secret-minting methods require CSPRNG' rule when they add the trait.

Bot's recommended 5-slice decomposition is no longer relevant — there is no work to decompose.

Cross-references:
  - JMAP-sc1b.101 (closed, the forward-looking placeholder this was supposed to close)
  - JMAP-cf7p (jmap-testjig epic, demonstrates that workspace integration testing needs SSE + WS, not §7.2)
  - workspace AGENTS.md 'What this workspace is' (to be added) — formalizes the kit-not-server posture this deferral honors
title: Implement PushSubscription server-side (RFC 8620 §7.2) — CSPRNG required for generate_verification_code
